item.title: Play the Cyber Bowl — Thu Oct 1
item.description:
It's time to play the third annual Cyber Bowl, a month-long competition to determine which North Carolina university is the most cyber savvy.
All October long, students, faculty and staff can log into the Cyber Bowl website and take a short cybersecurity quiz. Each completed quiz earns a point for Carolina.
UNC-Chapel Hill faces off against nine other North Carolina universities with a lot to prove and two wins to defend. In the inaugural Cyber Bowl, Carolina won the championship by garnering the largest participation by percentage. Last year, Carolina fielded the most players — almost 2,000 — of any school.
The Cyber Bowl is sponsored by Information Technology Services and the Information Security Office as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

item.title: ‘United States Diplomacy: From Its Beginnings to Today’ ADST Traveling Exhibition — Thu Oct 1, 7:30 AM — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
UNC Global Affairs is pleased to partner with the Association for Diplomatic Studies and Training (ADST) to host a traveling exhibition on the history of American diplomacy, “United States Diplomacy: From Its Beginnings to Today.”
Created with support from the Una Chapman Cox Foundation, the 21-panel exhibition celebrates diplomatic accomplishments and traces diplomacy’s role across America’s 250-year history, from Benjamin Franklin’s mission to Paris during the Revolutionary War, to 21st-century challenges such as transnational terrorism, climate change and global health.
The exhibition begins during the opening reception for Diplomacy Week 2026 on Monday, Sept. 28, and will be on display in the FedEx Global Education Center until Friday, Oct. 2.

item.description:
Art and Art History
Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering
August 20-October 15, 2026
Reception: August 20, 5-7 pm
Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. After searching for the perfect venue, they are thrilled to bring their collaborative installation to UNC. Their first public artwork, Turnabout Folly, will debut in Lansing, Michigan in Fall 2026.

item.title: Worlds of 1776: “The American Constitution: A Thousand-Year History?” — Thu Oct 1, 1:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
Join us for conversation with Professor Mark Peterson (Yale) about his new book The Making and Breaking of the American Constitution: A Thousand Year History.
This book charts the history and aims of the American constitution from its origins in an agrarian past to the grave crisis we face today. Peterson traces the American constitutional tradition to the control of land in medieval England, showing how the founders incorporated the aspirations of Magna Carta with the administrative principles of the Domesday Book, a meticulous survey and valuation of landed property commissioned by William the Conqueror. This framework encouraged the growth of democratic self-government but also institutionalized the colonization of territory and the expulsion of Indigenous peoples, establishing a legal blueprint for transforming tribal lands into revenue-yielding real estate for settlers. This workshop is offered by the University Libraries and will be led by librarian Michele Hayslett.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom only. You can register through the library calendar. Registrants will receive a Zoom link; those on the waitlist will not receive a Zoom link unless they are bumped up to a registered spot.

item.title: Fluid Master — Thu Oct 1, 5:00 PM — Center for Documentary Studies
item.description:
Can an oil change be filmed as a fluid master?
Join artist Kenya (Robinson) for a free public event exploring the surprising connections between documentary filmmaking and auto mechanics through a live, embodied performance.
In filmmaking, a "fluid master" is an entire scene captured in one continuous shot while the camera remains in motion. For this event, Kenya will perform two live oil changes as continuous fluid master shots, inviting participants to consider how routine automotive maintenance can be transformed through the language of filmmaking. As she works, Kenya will engage attendees in a conversation about her life and practice as a Black woman, fine artist, and mechanic.
Come view the action from multiple camera angles, including a live GoPro feed, while taking part in an artist talk that explores labor, performance, observation, and the stories embedded in everyday systems.

item.title: ‘Never A Bad Peace: Celebrating 250 Years of American Diplomacy’ with Adam Howard — Thu Oct 1, 5:30 PM — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
In 1783, Benjamin Franklin wrote, “May we never see another War! for in my Opinion there never was a good War, or a bad Peace.”
In this Diplomatic Discussion, the keynote lecture of Diplomacy Week 2026, Adam Howard, former chief historian at the U.S. Department of State, discusses three pivotal moments in American history shaped by the work of talented diplomats: the Revolutionary War, the Civil War and the aftermath of World War II.
Vice Provost for Global Affairs and Chief Global Officer Barbara Stephenson conducts a fireside chat, followed by questions from students in the audience. Afterwards, join Howard and Stephenson in the Florence and James Peacock Atrium for pizza and discussion.
Thursday, Oct. 1
5:30 p.m. (doors open at 5 p.m.)

item.description:
Film Screening:
"Sherman's March" (Ross McElwee, 1986, 158 min, USA, DCP)
Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman's 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South.
A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, "Sherman's March" sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross's deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross's mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel.

item.title: Día de los Muertos Ofrenda — Fri Oct 2 — Duke Chapel
item.description:
Honor the dead with Día de los Muertos Ofrenda, a Day of the Dead altar piece, at Duke Chapel. This year's Día de los Muertos Ofrenda at Duke Chapel features newly commissioned artwork by Ricky Armendariz, a Texas-based artist whose work explores the blend of Mexican, American, and Indigenous cultures along the U.S.-Mexico border. A collaboration with Duke Arts, Say the Thing and the Innovation Co-Lab, the installation incorporates a series of original panel designs by Armendariz, engraved at the Co-Lab and added to this year's Ofrenda.
Now in its fourth year, the Ofrenda returns as part of Duke Chapel's mission to bridge faith, learning, and community through art and shared remembrance. Visitors are invited to participate in this cherished Mexican tradition by contributing photographs, mementos, written tributes, or links to a communal paper chain honoring departed loved ones.
Visit the Ofrenda on your own or join us for special events leading up to Día de los Muertos on November 1

August 20-October 15, 2026

Drawn together in graduate school by their mutual love of experimentation and play, Michelle Inez Hinojosa and Barbara Pearsall have built a collaborative practice around analogue animation and vibrant abstraction. Together, their work explores optical toys, immersive installations, and movement. Under the Tent: Whirling & Flickering features kaleidoscopic imagery, flickering abstractions, projection mapping, a hidden trapdoor, and hand-cranked wheels that transform what viewers see. item.title: Swift Night Out (Charlotte) — Sun Oct 4, 6:45 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF, Mecklenburg Audubon Society, and NCWF Charlotte Wildlife Stewards Chapter to meet the most spectacular aerial insectivores, Chimney swifts. These birds spend almost their entire lives flying, hunting insects, and even bathing on the wing. Having lost much of their habitat to development, chimney swifts now rely on brick mason chimneys for survival. As the sun goes down and the swifts make their way home for the night, chat with local conservationists about chimney swift biology, behavior, and conservation. Discover their miraculous fall migration and observe swifts up close using scopes and binoculars. The night will culminate with the spectacle that is many hundreds of swifts chattering while swirling into a vortex before dropping into the chimney. Help us count the birds and contribute to their conservation efforts. REGISTER HERE
